title: Sweep-and-hold release playbook (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the "sweep-and-hold" tactic — an alternate canary approach where we briefly sweep a small set of cohorts to warm caches and then hold traffic while we observe stability signals before ramping. Not a formal team doc yet; experiment notes and decisions to capture.

High-level idea:
- Sweep: send brief bursts (5–15s) from 2–3 warmup cohorts to exercise critical code paths + KV/prefix cache.
- Hold: hold steady at a small fraction (0.1–0.5%) for an observation window (3–10 minutes) to detect slow regressions and memory/eviction churn.
- Ramp: gradually increase to target fraction with staggered cohort expansion and guardrails.

When to use:
- New model quantization changes (int8/int4)
- Kernel upgrades or new batching algorithm toggles
- Cache semantics changes (prefix cache invalidation, TTL changes)

Preflight checklist (local/console):
- [ ] CI green for runtime e2e and perf smoke (PR #1892)
- [ ] Canary image built and pinned in registry tag rlp-sweep-20241107
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured in last 24h (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, GPU mem)
- [ ] Alert hooks wired: slack #sre-ops, #prod-watch; pager on SLO breaches
- [ ] Canary cohorts registered in routing layer (cohort ids: sweep-A,B,C)
- [ ] Warmup workload script ready: tools/warmup/sweep-warmup.sh

Execution knobs (operational):
- initial_burst: 10s at 1 req/s per cohort (adjust for model cost)
- hold_fraction: 0.2% global traffic
- hold_window: 7m (can shorten to 3m if signal strong)
- step_ramp: double fraction every 10m up to target (max 60m total)

Traffic split example (api override):
- stable: 99.7%
- sweep-A: 0.1%
- sweep-B: 0.1%
- sweep-C: 0.1%

Monitoring & signals to watch (quick):
- correctness: content-quality checks (sampled eval set pass rate)
- latency: p95 and p99 delta vs baseline (>15% increase = yellow, >40% = red)
- errors: non-200 error-rate (>0.5% = yellow), 5xx spike = red
- GPU memory churn: evictions/ooms reported by exporter
- cache-hit ratio drop >10%
- token cost per request spike (unexpected token inflation)

Rollforward vs rollback decision tree (brief):
- soft anomaly (yellow): hold and extend hold_window, enable deeper traces for 10% of canary traffic
- hard anomaly (red): immediate pinback to stable model + route all cohorts back to stable; preserve canary logs and core dumps
- intermittent: move to canary-debug mode (capture full request/response for 0.5% traffic for 30m)

Pinning strategy notes:
- pin version at the routing layer (model_version + quantization_tag). Use immutable image tags.
- keep a mapping doc: release-tag -> model-hash -> runtime-image (update during preflight)
- when rolling back, ensure cookies/affinity cleared for cohorts that saw the bad variant

Housekeeping commands (examples):
- Update routing: curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/route/update -d '{"split":{"stable":0.997,"sweep-A":0.001,"sweep-B":0.001,"sweep-C":0.001}}'
- Pin image: ./ops/pin-version.sh rlp-sweep-20241107
- Start warmup: ./tools/warmup/sweep-warmup.sh --cohort A --duration 15s

Edge cases / gotchas I've seen:
- Warmup burst can trigger rate-limits on client side; coordinate with SDK teams for short-lived higher qps
- Cache warmup effect is non-linear; 10 warmup reqs might be enough for small prefix sets but not for longer context models
- Some telemetry pipelines sample heavily during burst windows -> might hide p99 signals; add dedicated tracing for canary cohorts

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add an automated job that runs sweep-and-hold preflight on every infra PR? (ticket: INF-4820?)
- Should we bake a "hold-mode" into the routing API to avoid repeated updates?
- Define standard observation window per change class (model, runtime, infra)

Post-run notes (template):
- start_time: 
- initial_burst_ok: yes/no + notes
- hold_window_metrics_snapshot: p50/p95/p99 + error-rate
- action_taken: ramped/held/rolled-back
- root_cause_hint:
- followups: (owners + jira ids)

If this works well, propose a small automation: single CLI that runs preflight, kicks sweep, collects snapshot, and produces a short report in Slack channel. For now, manual step-by-step until we iterate.

Slack / comms snippets (copyable):
- "Starting sweep-and-hold for rlp-sweep-20241107 — will do 3 warmup cohorts, hold 7m at 0.2% then step ramp. Watch #prod-watch. If any red signal, we pin-back immediately."
- "Rolled back rlp-sweep-20241107 after p99 spike + OOMs at 2024-11-07T14:12Z — collecting logs and core dumps (INF-4723)"

Notes to self: keep the heuristics conservative first two runs. Capture everything (traces + full request samples for a tiny fraction)."
